title: How to Wash Wool Without Shrinking It

seo.title: How to Wash Wool Without Shrinking It
seo.meta_description: Wash wool without shrinking or felting it by following the label, using a wool or gentle cycle, mild detergent, minimal agitation, and flat drying.
seo.search_intent: Wash wool garments while minimizing shrinkage, felting, and stretching.

excerpt: Wool does not shrink simply because it touches water. The bigger risk is the combination of moisture, heat, and agitation. The care label matters: some modern wool is machine washable, while other garments require hand washing or professional cleaning.
content_html:
The idea that all wool shrinks the moment it gets wet is too simple. The real risk rises when moisture, heat, and friction encourage wool fibers to interlock and felt. That is why two wool sweaters can have completely different care instructions.

Start with the care label

Some wool can go in the washer, some is hand-wash only, and some is dry-clean only. If machine washing is allowed, use the wool setting; when there is no wool cycle, a cold delicate cycle may be appropriate if the manufacturer permits it.

Woolmark notes that many machine-washable wool garments can be cleaned safely on a wool program and recommends a mild, neutral detergent.

Avoid temperature shocks and unnecessary movement

Do not scrub or wring. For hand washing, use lukewarm water or the temperature on the label and move the garment as little as necessary. Woolmark suggests about 30°C/86°F for many hand-wash wool items and a short soak.

Use detergent made for the job

A mild wool detergent is less likely to be harsh on the fiber. Measure it rather than pouring extra; too much soap does not protect wool and makes rinsing harder.

Remove water without stretching

Support the garment's weight when lifting it. Do not pick up a soaked sweater by one shoulder. Gently press out water, then roll the garment in a clean towel and press if needed.

Dry sweaters flat

Drying can cause as much distortion as washing. Woolmark recommends flat drying many knit garments so the weight of retained water does not pull them longer. Gently reshape the body, sleeves, and neckline before leaving the sweater to dry.

Avoid radiators, high dryer heat, and harsh direct sun. Some wool items specifically labeled for tumble drying can use a compatible setting, but follow that label exactly.

If the garment already shrank

A piece that is merely misshapen may recover somewhat when dampened and gently reshaped. True felting—where the fabric has become denser, thicker, and more compact—may not be fully reversible.

Prevention is easier than rescue

Do not guess at temperature or drying. When you are unsure whether to use wool, delicate, or hand wash, return to the label. The goal is gentle cleaning with minimal friction, followed by drying that does not add heat or stretch.

faq.question: Can wool go in a washing machine?
faq.answer: Some wool garments can, when the care label allows it and the correct wool or gentle cycle is used.

faq.question: What temperature should wool be washed at?
faq.answer: Follow the label. Many hand-wash wool garments use lukewarm water around 30°C/86°F.

faq.question: Can I hang a wet wool sweater to dry?
faq.answer: Flat drying is usually safer for knits because hanging wet wool can stretch it.
